answer.rationale: The finance mandate (18% cut) combined with incumbent's refusal to renegotiate, expiring contract in 14 days without auto-renewal, and the low-cost vendor's quote meeting the mandate create a time-constrained forcing function. Memory_c2 demonstrates that the low-cost vendor delivered sharp unit cost cuts with quick onboarding and accurate invoicing in a previous cycle. Memory_c4 shows that renegotiation can recover margin, but the incumbent has already refused this cycle, eliminating that option. Memory_c6 indicates multi-year commitments unlock better pricing, but we lack the budget flexibility to renew at current terms. With 94% line utilization (no buffer for supply disruption), this decision carries delivery risk. Switching to the low-cost vendor on a standard-experiment scale (not full broad rollout) allows us to meet the mandate while monitoring for any degradation in performance or reliability. The low-cost vendor's prior track record and proven ability to scale quickly reduce but do not eliminate risk. Deferring is not viable given the 14-day hard deadline and auto-renewal expiration.
